entities.summary:
Andrea di Bonaiuto da Firenze or Andrea da Firenze was an Italian painter active in Florence from approximately 1340 to 1379. He was a prominent figure in the Early Renaissance, known for his lyrical and harmonious style. Andrea's most notable works include the 'Annunciation' and 'The Holy Family with Saint John the Baptist', which showcase his mastery of composition and color palette.

Born in Florence, Italy around 1340, Andrea di Bonaiuto was the son of a wealthy merchant family. He received his artistic training from the renowned artist Giotto, who had a significant influence on his style. Andrea's work was heavily influenced by the artistic movements of the time, including the International Gothic style.

Andrea di Bonaiuto's artistic legacy extends beyond his own works, as he played a significant role in shaping the artistic identity of Florence. He was a key figure in the development of the city's unique artistic style, which blended elements of Gothic and Renaissance art. Andrea's work also had a lasting impact on the art world, influencing artists such as Fra Angelico and Sandro Botticelli.
